title: Pollack's unhappy end; leaving for Paris and Zez Confrey
summary: Freeman declines to discuss Pollack's end, then says he left the band after a year in 1928 for Paris, found the music bad, and joined Zez Confrey in Chicago.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: Well, we're not, we're on to Ben Pollack.

We are on to Ben Pollack, of course, but I was thinking for a second, as you said that, as regards Pollack, I think the things that caused his unhappy ending are not things that I want to talk about. They could certainly easily offend people who might be related to him. The only thing I know is that Pollack was a wonderful man --
We did talk an awful lot about him.
All right. Good. Do you want to say anything more about the Pollack band, anybody in it, or --
I was only in the band about, I think, less than a year certainly. Only in the band about a year and then I had a chance to go to Paris and I went over and I was very disillusioned with that.
Why, this was what, in the 30 whats?

Well, I over to Paris -- Dave Tough, my good friend was over there and I went over to have a look at it and then found that the bands -- the music would be bad, so I came back and went right out to Chicago and got a job with Zez Confrey. That was kind of a funny thing because Zez was not a jazz pianist, but he was a good composer, he wrote all those, Kitten on the Keys.
